raw_segments.text: I have already spoken of the natural defects of democratic institutions, and they all of
them increase at the exact ratio of the power of the majority.
To begin with the most evident of them all, the mutability of the laws is an evil inherent
in democratic government, because it is natural to democracies to raise men to power in very
But this evil is more or less sensible in proportion to the authority and the means
of action which the legislature possesses.
